Ticking one or more limits this account to those groups' machines everywhere — lists, search, actions, scheduling, and the AI assistant. strings.users.edit.reset_password_confirm: Reset this user's password and sign them out everywhere?

strings.users.new.email_hint: Optional — the address notification rules send to when they target this user (see Notifications). Not used for login.
strings.users.new.username_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'. This is also the LDAP username and the OIDC identity, if used.
strings.users.new.auth_provider_hint: "local": a password set below. "ldap"/"oidc": leave the password field empty — the username is matched against the directory/provider instead (see Settings).
strings.users.new.password_hint: At least 12 characters. Required for "local" accounts, left blank otherwise. The user must change it on first login.
strings.users.new.api_access_label: API access — allows this user to create and use their own API tokens
strings.users.new.restrict_groups_label: Restrict this account to specific machine groups

Ticking one or more limits this account to those groups' machines everywhere — lists, search, actions, scheduling, and the AI assistant. Machines in no group stay hidden from a restricted account, and "All machines" isn't available to it as a scheduling target. The audit log is never restricted.

strings.machine.host_key_pinned_hint: The connection will be refused if the server ever presents a different key.
strings.machine.host_key_missing_hint: This machine doesn't have a confirmed host key fingerprint yet — until it does, no connection can be safely established (no automatic "trust on first use"), and facts can't be gathered. Discovery runs automatically below; you still have to confirm the fingerprint yourself once it's shown, after checking it through a channel outside this app.
strings.machine.confirm_key_first: Confirm the server's key fingerprint above first.
strings.machine.facts.heading: Facts
strings.machine.facts.not_gathered_yet: Not gathered yet — this happens automatically once the host key fingerprint is confirmed above, and refreshes periodically after that.
strings.machine.host_key.discovery_error: Could not determine the key fingerprint: {error}
strings.machine.host_key.presents: The server presents this key fingerprint:
strings.machine.host_key.verify_hint: Before confirming it, verify it through a different, trusted channel — e.g. directly on the hosting provider's console, or by running ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub on the machine itself. If it doesn't match, do NOT confirm — this could be a Man-in-the-Middle attack.
strings.machine.packages.not_gathered_yet: Not gathered yet — this happens automatically once the host key fingerprint is confirmed above, and refreshes periodically after that (and right after any update run on this machine).

strings.monitoring.not_gathered_yet: Not gathered yet — this happens automatically once the host key fingerprint is confirmed on the Overview tab, and refreshes periodically after that (every {interval} {seconds}).
strings.monitoring.truncated_hint: This machine has more samples in this window than can be shown at once — the graphs below cover the most recent samples rather than the full range. Pick a shorter range, or shorten the retention window in Settings.
strings.monitoring.disk.no_usage_data: No filesystem usage data in this range.
strings.monitoring.availability.heading: Availability
strings.machine.edit.readiness_password_hint: Run "Run initial setup" below to fix this.
strings.machine.edit.readiness_root_hint: This machine already connects as root — nothing needs sudo access it doesn't already have. The credential already on file is enough to install what's missing directly, no login needed.
strings.machine.edit.readiness_sudoers_hint: Add this sudoers rule yourself over your own SSH session (then click "Re-check" below) — often the only option, since password SSH to a privileged account is commonly disabled by policy:
strings.machine.edit.let_debcontrol_do_it: Or let debcontrol do it (needs a one-time root/sudo login)
strings.machine.edit.let_debcontrol_do_it_hint: This machine already uses debcontrol's own SSH key for everyday use — fixing the items above needs a root-equivalent login just this once, the same as the original setup did. Nothing is stored afterward; on success this machine goes right back to using its own SSH key. This won't work if password SSH to that account is disabled — use the manual command above instead.
strings.machine.edit.temp_connect_confirm: Temporarily connect as this account to fix what's missing, then switch back to debcontrol's own SSH key?
strings.machine.edit.ip_change_hint: Changing the IP address or port resets the pinned host key fingerprint and gathered facts below — you'll need to re-discover and re-confirm the fingerprint before connecting again.
strings.machine.edit.ssh_key_hint_after: for the app's SSH public key.
strings.machine.edit.password_unchanged_placehol: Leave empty to keep the current password unchanged.
strings.machine.edit.password_only_used_placehol: Only used if 'Password' is selected above.
strings.machine.edit.tags_hint: Comma-separated. Independent of the group above — a machine can carry any number.
strings.machine.edit.runbook_placeholder: How to deal with this server, who owns it, anything worth knowing…
strings.machine.edit.runbook_hint: Markdown supported. Shown on the Overview tab.
strings.machine.edit.active_label: Active (included in reachability checks and facts refresh)
strings.machine.edit.overwrite_intervals_hint: Leave blank to use the instance-wide default set in .env. Only a larger value than the default actually changes anything — both sweeps still run at the global cadence, a machine with a longer interval is just skipped on ticks that come too soon.
strings.machine.edit.monitoring_retention_hint_b: This one isn't a sweep interval — it just picks how long this machine's samples are kept before the daily retention purge deletes them, overriding the instance-wide default set in
strings.machine.edit.confirm_key_overview_first: Confirm the server's key fingerprint on the Overview tab first.
strings.machine.edit.onboarding_hint: Prepares this machine the same way the wiki page "Ansible Onboarding"'s playbook would, run directly over SSH instead: creates a dedicated "debcontrol" user, installs this app's own SSH public key into it, grants it passwordless sudo scoped to apt-get/shutdown (and flatpak/snap, if either is installed), and installs ncurses-term (colors/box-drawing in the Terminal tab — best-effort, never blocks the rest). The password above must belong to root, or an account that already behaves like root — there is no sudo escalation to fall back on here. On success this machine switches to using debcontrol's own SSH key, and the password above is discarded.
strings.machine.edit.setup_completed: Setup completed — this machine now uses debcontrol's own SSH key.
strings.machine.edit.run_onboarding_confirm: Create a "debcontrol" user, grant it scoped sudo, and switch this machine to debcontrol's own SSH key?
strings.machine.new.hostname_hint: The machine's own hostname is discovered automatically once its SSH host key is confirmed — no need to enter it here.
strings.machine.new.auth_hint_before: SSH key uses debcontrol's own shared identity — see
strings.machine.new.auth_hint_after: for the public key to add to the machine's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. Password is only there as a fallback; prefer the key above whenever possible.
strings.machine.new.password_placeholder: Only used if 'Password' is selected above. Stored encrypted.
strings.machine.import.heading: Bulk import machines
strings.machine.import.csv_hint_before: Paste CSV with a header row — ip_address is required, hostname is optional and anything else is ignored. Rows become pending machines in the same review queue self-registration uses (see
strings.machine.import.csv_hint_after: ) — no credentials or host keys are set here, so each one still needs the normal add-machine form and host-key confirmation before debcontrol connects to it.
strings.machine.config_import.title: Import configuration
strings.machine.config_import.heading: Import machine & group configuration
strings.machine.config_import.hint1_after: ("Export config (JSON)"). This creates real machines and groups directly — it is not the pending-review queue bulk import uses, so it's meant for restoring/migrating already-known configuration, not discovering unknown hosts.
strings.machine.config_import.hint2: This is a structural export/import, not a credentials backup: it never contains (or restores) a machine's password/key material or its pinned SSH host-key fingerprint. A machine originally using password authentication is imported with "SSH key" instead (there's nothing to re-import) — its name is called out below so you can revisit its credentials. Every imported machine starts with no pinned host key, exactly like a freshly hand-added one — use "Discover key fingerprint" and confirm it before anything connects to it.
strings.machine.config_import.hint3: A machine whose name already exists is skipped, not overwritten — this never changes an existing machine's connection details.
strings.machine.config_import.auth_warning: These machine(s) originally used password authentication and were imported as "SSH key" instead — revisit their credentials:
strings.machine.package_search.hint: Search installed packages across every machine at once — e.g. after a CVE announcement, find every machine that still has a vulnerable version installed. Reflects each machine's last package refresh (see the "Installed packages" panel on a machine's own page); it doesn't connect to anything live.
strings.machine.package_search.truncated: Showing the first {count} matches — narrow the search (or pick a source) to see the rest.
strings.machine.package_search.no_match: No machine has a package matching "{query}".
strings.machine.logs.title: Logs
strings.machine.terminal.title: Terminal
strings.machine.terminal.hint: Connecting as {username} ({ip}). This is a full interactive shell — whatever that account (and its sudo rights, if any) can do, you can do here. The session ends automatically after a few hours of use, and immediately if you close this tab.
strings.machine.power.command_sent: {action} command sent — the status on the Overview tab will reflect it once it takes effect.
strings.machine.power.hint: Requires root/sudo, same as system updates. Both ask you to type the machine's name to confirm before doing anything.
strings.machine.power_confirm.effect_reboot: it will restart and be briefly unreachable.
strings.machine.power_confirm.effect_shutdown: it will power off and stay unreachable until someone turns it back on.
strings.machine.power_confirm.type_name: Type the machine's name ({name}) to confirm
strings.machine.bulk_power_confirm.body: This sends {command} to each selected machine that has a confirmed host key fingerprint (others are skipped) — immediately, no going back once sent.
strings.machine.updates.hint: Always runs apt-get update, then the selected upgrade strategy, then autoremove and autoclean (the cleanup steps run regardless of whether the upgrade step succeeded) — and, if installed, flatpak update and snap refresh too. Requires root for apt — either the configured user is root, or has passwordless sudo for apt-get (and, recommended, flatpak/snap too). See the wiki page "Managed Machine Requirements" for a sudoers example.
strings.machine.updates.preview_hint: Shows exactly what would happen — including anything autoremove would remove — before anything actually runs.
strings.machine.updates.no_runs_match: No update runs match this filter.
strings.machine.preview.title: Preview update
strings.machine.preview.heading: Preview update for {name}
strings.machine.preview.simulated_hint: Simulated with apt's dry-run mode (apt-get -s) — nothing on {name} has changed yet. This is exactly what {strategy} followed by autoremove would do; review it, then confirm below to actually run it.
strings.machine.preview.to_remove_warning: This is the risky part of autoremove — double-check nothing here is something you still need.
strings.machine.preview.to_install_heading: Packages that would be installed or upgraded ({count})
strings.machine.preview.nothing_installed: Nothing would be installed or upgraded.
strings.machine.preview.nothing_pending: Nothing is pending — apt-get update and the cleanup steps will still run if you confirm, same as clicking "Run update" always has, but there's nothing for the upgrade step to do.
strings.machine.update_run.title: Update run
strings.machine.availability.not_checked_yet: Not checked yet. This runs automatically on the same periodic sweep as facts, whenever you click "Check for updates now" below, and whenever a scheduled "Check for updates" task fires (see the Scheduling tab) — whichever ran last is what's shown here, including the package names.
strings.machine.availability.last_check_failed: Last check (checked {when}) couldn't determine what's available via apt — see the error above, or try again. (flatpak/snap checks below don't depend on this.)
strings.machine.availability.reboot_needed_hint: a newer kernel is installed but not yet running
strings.machine.update_run.waiting_for_output: Waiting for output — this refreshes automatically.
strings.machine.update_run.rollback_confirm: Re-install the exact package versions from before this update? Only packages whose version has since changed are touched.
strings.machine.update_run.rollback_hint: Re-installs the package versions captured right before this update ran, for whatever has since changed. Needs the old .deb still resolvable from a configured apt source — otherwise apt reports it can't locate that version, same as any other apt failure.
strings.machine.update_run.is_rollback: This is a rollback of an earlier update run.

strings.scheduling.config_import.hint2: A scheduled task's name isn't unique, so this always creates a new task — running the same import twice creates two identical schedules. Delete the old ones by hand first if that's not what you want.
strings.scheduling.run_enqueued: Run enqueued — check the machine/group/batch page shortly.
strings.scheduling.target_hint: Machines without a pinned host key fingerprint are silently skipped when the schedule fires, same as the manual buttons.
strings.scheduling.target_restricted_hint: Your account is restricted to specific machine groups, so "All machines" isn't available as a target.
strings.scheduling.cron_hint: Standard 5-field cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, always interpreted in UTC. E.g.

strings.ai.title: AI assistant
strings.ai.intro_before_confirm: Describe what you want in plain language. The assistant can look up your machines and groups on its own, and can propose actions against them — updates, reboots, or a shell command. Nothing it proposes ever runs until you read the exact command and target list and click
strings.ai.intro_after_confirm: . It can only propose what your own role already allows you to do by hand.
strings.ai.model_hint: A conversation stays on the model it was started with.
strings.ai.first_message_placeholder: e.g. install apache2 on the group web-servers
strings.ai.no_model_enabled: No AI model is enabled yet.
strings.ai.configure_provider_hint_before: Configure a provider, fetch its models, and tick the ones to allow on the

strings.ai.privacy_hint_before: Conversations are private to your own account — nobody else, including administrators, can read them. Anything you actually confirm still shows up in the
strings.ai.chat.command_label: Command, exactly as it will run:
strings.ai.chat.skipped_unpinned: Skipped (no confirmed SSH host key fingerprint):
strings.ai.chat.read_before_confirming: Read the command and the target list above before confirming. Nothing has run yet.
strings.ai.chat.no_messages_yet: No messages yet — ask something below.

strings.ai.chat.waiting_for_reply: Waiting for the assistant's reply — this updates automatically.

Turning this on skips that step for anything the assistant proposes next — every further command runs the moment it's proposed, with no chance to review it first. Only for this conversation, only in this browser tab: it turns off the moment you leave or close it, and every other conversation still asks as normal.
strings.ai.chat.auto_confirm_toggle: Auto-confirm further commands in this conversation
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity_hint: debcontrol connects to machines using this one shared key when "SSH key" is chosen as the authentication method — there's no key upload/generation to do per machine. To let it manage a machine, append the public key below to that machine's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for the user debcontrol will connect as. Adding it to an already-managed machine can be done for you — see "Push pending key to all machines" below once you've generated a replacement key.
strings.settings.general.pending_key_generated_b: A replacement key was generated {generated_at} and is
strings.settings.general.pending_key_generated_a: . Append it to every managed machine's authorized_keys too (alongside the current one, don't remove the old line yet) before activating — activating switches which key debcontrol uses immediately, and any machine that hasn't got the new line yet will become unreachable.
strings.settings.general.push_result_partial: See the errors above for the rest.
strings.settings.general.push_key: Push pending key to all machines
strings.settings.general.push_key_hint: "Push pending key to all machines" runs a command over SSH (using each machine's currently active key) to append the pending key above to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys — for every machine using "SSH key" authentication with a pinned host key. It does not remove the old line or activate anything; it only saves you the manual copy-paste step above. Machines using password authentication aren't affected, since they don't use this key at all.
strings.settings.checks.reachability_check_hint: How often each machine is pinged.
strings.settings.checks.facts_refresh_hint: How often OS/package facts are refreshed.
strings.settings.checks.monitoring_sample_hint: How often CPU/RAM/disk usage is sampled.
strings.settings.checks.reachability_concurrency: How many machines to check at once.
strings.settings.checks.ssh_connect_timeout_hint: Max wait when opening an SSH connection.
strings.settings.checks.update_timeout_hint: Max time to wait for an update run to finish.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks_hint: Timeout and concurrency changes apply immediately. Interval changes need a worker/beat restart.
strings.settings.security.audit_hash_chain_hint: Every entry is hash-chained (each links to the previous one's hash), so altering or removing an entry breaks the chain from that point on — see Audit and the wiki page "Architecture" for how that works and what it doesn't protect against.
strings.settings.security.keep_audit_days_hint: Leave empty to keep every entry forever (the default). Otherwise, entries older than this are permanently deleted once a day — the chain's most recent entries and its ability to verify what remains are unaffected, since only the oldest end is ever pruned.
strings.settings.security.export_hint_before: Every entry can also be exported for archival/compliance outside the app:
strings.settings.security.export_hint_after: (the Audit page's own export links respect whatever search/outcome filter is set there).
strings.settings.security.geoip_hint: Resolves a public source IP to a country/city on every new audit log entry — a MaxMind-DB-format (.mmdb) database this app downloads itself (never bundled; MaxMind's GeoLite2 license forbids redistribution). A machine's own LAN address, or a login through an internal reverse proxy, has no real-world location and is never looked up.
strings.settings.security.geoip_url_hint: A direct download link to a .mmdb, .mmdb.gz, or .tar.gz file — e.g. a MaxMind GeoLite2 "permalink" (embeds your license key, kept encrypted at rest like every other secret here).
strings.settings.checks.dashboard_trends_hint: One daily snapshot of fleet-wide counts, for the Dashboard trend chart. Only affects retention, not live counts.
strings.settings.checks.update_run_hint: Stored apt/flatpak/snap output per run. Doesn't affect scheduled updates or the audit log.
strings.settings.checks.monitoring_history_hint: Only affects retention, not sampling frequency (set above).
strings.settings.checks.monitoring_downsampling_: Thins out old samples instead of deleting them — charts already bucket old data for display, so this saves storage without losing trend shape.
strings.settings.integrations.syslog_hint: Live-mirrors every audit log entry to an external syslog server (e.g. a SIEM) as it's written — RFC 5424 formatted, best-effort: a delivery failure here is only ever logged, never blocks the action being audited. The database entry (exportable on the Security tab) is always the real record; this is just a copy sent elsewhere.
strings.settings.integrations.smtp_hint: Configuration only, for now — nothing in the app sends an email through this yet. Lets the relay be set up and saved ahead of an actual notification feature. Same encrypted-secret convention as LDAP/OIDC below.
strings.settings.integrations.ldap_hint_before: When enabled, a user set to login method "ldap" (see
strings.settings.integrations.ldap_hint_after: ) logs in with the same username/password form as a local account — the username is looked up in the directory below, and their password is checked against it, not against anything stored here.
strings.settings.integrations.use_starttls: Use StartTLS (only relevant for a plain "ldap://" server URI)
strings.settings.integrations.tls_verify_hint: Only for "ldaps://" or StartTLS. Turn off only if you know this directory's certificate is self-signed or otherwise won't validate and you still want to use it — with it off, any certificate is accepted, with no protection against a machine-in-the-middle.
strings.settings.integrations.leave_blank_hint: Leave blank to keep the current value unchanged.
strings.settings.integrations.user_search_filter: Must contain {username}. Typical OpenLDAP: (uid={username}). Active Directory: (sAMAccountName={username}).
strings.settings.integrations.provider_name_hint: Shown on the login button ("Log in with" + this name) instead of the generic "OIDC" — purely cosmetic, e.g. "Entra ID", "Authentik", "Google Workspace". Blank keeps the generic label.
strings.settings.integrations.oidc_hint_before: When enabled, the login page shows a "Log in with OIDC" button. A user set to login method "oidc" (see
strings.settings.integrations.oidc_hint_after: ) is matched by comparing their username against the claim named below in the ID token the provider returns — nothing is auto-created from this.
strings.settings.integrations.issuer_url_hint: Must serve /.well-known/openid-configuration (standard for any OIDC provider — Keycloak, Authentik, Entra ID, Okta, Google, ...). Paste the plain issuer URL here, not the full discovery URL — debcontrol appends /.well-known/openid-configuration itself.
strings.settings.integrations.redirect_uri_hint: Register this exact redirect URI with the provider:
strings.settings.ai.intro_after: page. Enabling a provider isn't the same as trusting its whole catalog: fetch its models, then tick exactly which ones may be picked for a conversation. Everything the assistant can actually do against a machine is still gated by the requesting user's own role permissions, and every action it proposes must be confirmed by a human before it runs.
strings.settings.ai.base_url_hint: Required when this provider is enabled. Must expose the OpenAI /models and /chat/completions endpoints.
strings.settings.ai.token_limits_hint_before: Global ceilings on total tokens (input + output, all providers together) spent by the AI assistant in a
strings.settings.ai.token_limits_hint_after: window — the last 24 hours, 7 days, and 30 days respectively, not calendar days/weeks/months. A limit that is already reached blocks the next chat turn before any provider call is made. Leave empty for no limit.
strings.settings.ai.fleet_summary_hint_before: A background job writes a plain-language "what changed, what needs attention" report to the
strings.settings.ai.fleet_summary_hint_middle: — off by default, since (unlike everything else above) this makes a real AI API call on a schedule, whether or not anyone reads it. This only ever
strings.settings.ai.fleet_summary_hint_after: a report; add a rule for it in Notifications to also get emailed when a new one is ready.
strings.settings.ai.enable_provider_first: Enable a provider and choose at least one model above first.
